The reader's premise is false: the graph has an edge for this construct. It is attributed to the correct start screen: n_projects_projectId_translations -> u_n_projects_projectId_translations ('dynamic target from /projects/:projectId/translations', kind unknown, modality unknown), witness project-locales.component.html:17:36. The soundiness file also records it as 'fully dynamic navigation target'. The site was read and its scope is right, so this is neither (b), which preregistration defines as 'no construct for it in the graph', nor (a). Both screens exist, so it is not (c). The real cause is unresolved target resolution. The relative one-element array [routerLink]="[locale.locale.code]" sits in the #searchResultsItem ng-template under ProjectLocalesComponent (route 'translations', not an empty path, so legacy relativeLinkResolution does not apply). It resolves to translations/<code>, which matches translations/:localeCode. The extractor sent it to an unknown node, and the scorer does not count edges into non-screen nodes.

Same trigger and the same primary cause as the translations pair. The graph holds an edge for project-locales.component.html:17, but only into the unknown node u_n_projects_projectId_translations, because the dynamic relative target [locale.locale.code] is left unresolved. That is not (b). A second factor exists: /projects/:projectId is a redirect-only route (projects.module.ts:48, '' redirectTo 'translations', pathMatch full). ProjectLocalesComponent is routed only on /projects/:projectId/translations, so the edge starts at the translations screen and not at the :projectId screen. Even with the target resolved, the pair would need the redirect source to be credited with its redirect target's triggers. The miss therefore has two causes, an unresolved dynamic target plus a redirect-only start route, which the single-cause classes do not fit.
